name: Babysit a pull request
description: Watch one pull request until it is green and clean: poll CI and review feedback, hand each round of failures to a harness that fixes them at the root and pushes, and stop when nothing actionable is left or the round cap is hit.

inputs.name: pr
inputs.description: Pull request number or URL to babysit.

inputs.name: repo
inputs.description: owner/name to target. Empty means the checkout's own remote.

inputs.name: cwd
inputs.description: Checkout to run gh and the fixing harness in, relative to the workspace.

inputs.name: feedback_command
inputs.description: Optional command collecting review feedback. It must print JSON carrying `unresolvedThreads` and `changesRequested` counts, and it can read $PR and $REPO from the environment — e.g. `pr-comments "$PR" --json -R "$REPO"`. The inspect step runs as a login shell, so the operator's own PATH and helper scripts are in scope. Empty falls back to `gh pr view`, which sees review verdicts but not thread resolution state.

args.script:
set -u
repo_arg=""
[ -n "${REPO:-}" ] && repo_arg="--repo ${REPO}"

# Reading the pull request is the one thing this step cannot fail quietly at:
# a missing `gh`, a stale token, or the wrong repo would otherwise yield an
# empty document that `assess` reads as "nothing to do" and reports green. So
# this one is fatal, and says which pull request it could not read.
if ! pr=$(gh pr view "$PR" $repo_arg --json number,title,url,state,isDraft,mergeable,mergeStateStatus,reviewDecision,headRefName 2>&1); then
  printf 'cannot read pull request %s: %s\n' "$PR" "$pr" >&2
  exit 1
fi

# `gh pr checks` exits non-zero when checks are failing or pending, which is
# exactly the case this node exists to report — so its status is ignored and
# only its output is read. `bucket` is what collapses GitHub's dozen states
# into pass/fail/pending/skipping/cancel; classifying on raw `state` misses
# ACTION_REQUIRED and EXPECTED, which block a merge while looking like
# neither a failure nor a pending run.
checks=$(gh pr checks "$PR" $repo_arg --json name,state,bucket,link 2>/dev/null || true)
[ -n "$checks" ] || checks='[]'

if [ -n "${FEEDBACK_COMMAND:-}" ]; then
  # `shell: "user"` with `shell_args: ["-l"]` above made this the operator's
  # own login shell, so their PATH and helper scripts (`pr-comments` and
  # friends) are already on hand.
  feedback=$(eval "$FEEDBACK_COMMAND" 2>/dev/null || true)
else
  feedback=$(gh pr view "$PR" $repo_arg --json reviewDecision,reviews,comments -q '{unresolvedThreads: 0, changesRequested: (if .reviewDecision == "CHANGES_REQUESTED" then 1 else 0 end), detail: .}' 2>/dev/null || true)
fi
[ -n "$feedback" ] || feedback='{}'

printf '{"checks":%s,"pr":%s,"feedback":%s}\n' "$checks" "$pr" "$feedback"

config.prompt:
="Pull request " + (.nodes.assess.item.pr.url // ("#" + (.nodes.assess.item.pr.number | tostring))) + " on branch " + (.nodes.assess.item.pr.headRefName // "?") + " is not ready.

Failing checks:
" + (.nodes.assess.item.failing | tostring) + "

Review feedback:
" + (.nodes.assess.item.feedback | tostring) + "

This is round " + (.nodes.watch.iteration | tostring) + " of 8. Check out that branch, fix every failure at its root, and push. Never skip hooks, never disable or weaken a test, and never force a check green. Reply to and resolve each review thread you address, and say plainly which ones you are declining and why."

args.script:
set -u
# Nothing is actionable. If checks are still running, sleeping before the
# next poll is the whole point of the round; if none are, this settles.
if [ "${PENDING:-0}" != "0" ]; then sleep 60; fi
printf '{"settled":%s}\n' "$([ "${PENDING:-0}" = "0" ] && echo true || echo false)"
